title: Tumoral and normal brain tissue extraction protocol for screening of organic pollutants
author: Gutiérrez-Martín, Marquès, et al.
materials: Instrumental analysis was performed in an Acquity UHPLC system (Waters, Milford, USA) coupled to a Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass analyser (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Dreieich, Germany) by means of an electrospray ionization interface (ESI) in positive (ESI+) and negative (ESI-) modes. The chromatography and mass spectrometry parameters are described as follows:I.Liquid chromatography•Column: Waters Cortecs C18 (2.1 × 100 mm, 2.7 μm)•Precolumn: Waters Cortecs C18 (2.1 × 5 mm, 2.7 μm)•Sample injected volume: 10 μl•Column temperature: 40 °C•Positive ionization mode (ESI+):-Mobile phase A: 0.1% formic acid in methanol-Mobile phase B: 0.1% formic acid in water-Gradient: (%A): Initial 5%, 75% at 7 min, 100% at 10 min, 100% at 15 min, 5% at 17 min and 5% at 23 min.•Negative ionization mode (ESI-):-Mobile phase A: 5 mM ammonium acetate in methanol-Mobile phase B: 5 mM ammonium acetate in water-Gradient: (%A): Initial 5%, 50% at 3 min, 90% at 6 min, 100% at 13 min, 100% at 17 min, 5% at 18 min, and 5% at 20 min.II.Mass spectrometry•Spray voltage: 3000 V (ESI+) and 2800 V (ESI-)•Capillary temperature: 350 °C•Sheath gas: 40•Auxiliary gas flow: 10•Max. Spray current: 100•Probe heater temperature: 350 °C•S-Lens RF Level: 60

steps.title: Configure LC-HRMS Instrumental Setup
steps.instruction: Set up an Acquity UHPLC system (Waters, Milford, USA) coupled to a Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass analyser (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Dreieich, Germany) using an electrospray ionization (ESI) interface.

substeps.instruction: Install a Waters Cortecs C18 column (2.1 × 100 mm, 2.7 μm) and a Waters Cortecs C18 precolumn (2.1 × 5 mm, 2.7 μm).
Set the sample injection volume to 10 μl.

steps.title: Set Liquid Chromatography Parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the mobile phases and gradients based on the required ionization mode.

substeps.instruction: For Positive Ionization Mode (ESI+): Use Mobile phase A (0.1% formic acid in methanol) and Mobile phase B (0.1% formic acid in water). Set gradient (%A): Initial 5%, 75% at 7 min, 100% at 10 min, 100% at 15 min, 5% at 17 min, and 5% at 23 min.

For Negative Ionization Mode (ESI-): Use Mobile phase A (5 mM ammonium acetate in methanol) and Mobile phase B (5 mM ammonium acetate in water). Set gradient (%A): Initial 5%, 50% at 3 min, 90% at 6 min, 100% at 13 min, 100% at 17 min, 5% at 18 min, and 5% at 20 min.

steps.title: Configure Mass Spectrometry Settings
steps.instruction: Adjust the mass spectrometer parameters for the ESI interface and data acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Set spray voltage to 3000 V for ESI+ and 2800 V for ESI-.
Set capillary temperature to 350 °C and probe heater temperature to 350 °C.
Set sheath gas to 40, auxiliary gas flow to 10, and max spray current to 100.
Operate the instrument in data independent acquisition (DIA) mode, consisting of a full scan with low collision energy and a full scan with high collision energy (25 eV).
Set the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) range from 67 to 1000 with a resolving power of 60,000.

steps.title: Perform Method Validation
steps.instruction: Evaluate the performance of the methodology using a set of 66 target chemicals (pharmaceuticals, PFAS, biocides, UV-Filters, plastic additives, food related chemicals, anticorrosion agents, and flame retardants).

substeps.instruction: Assess linearity by creating a calibration curve spiked at 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100 µg L−1 in a pooled sample of brain (final extract).

Evaluate matrix effect by preparing the same calibration curve (0.1, 0.5, 1, 10, 50, 100 µg L−1) in solvent (water/methanol, 1:1, v/v) and calculating the ratio of the slope in matrix to the slope in solvent.
Determine recovery (R%) by spiking a pooled sample at two concentration levels (5 and 20 µg L−1 theoretical concentration in vial) and processing 3 matrix blanks without standard addition.
Estimate limits of quantification (LOQ) as the lowest observable peak in the matrix calibration curve, and set limits of detection (LODs) as 3/10 of the LOQs.

description: A set of 66 chemicals were employed to evaluate the performance of the methodology, and the results are summarized in Table 1. These chemicals included pharmaceuticals, PFAS, biocides, UV-Filters, plastic additives, food related chemicals, anticorrosion agents, and flame retardants with different physicochemical properties (LogP in the range: −0.2 to 6.3). The proposed protocol has been validated in brain samples with a composite sample of brain by using the aforementioned 66 target chemicals . Due to the wide range of physicochemical properties of the selected compounds, this method is appropriate for non-target analysis.The following quality control parameters were assessed:•Linearity. The linearity and linear range were evaluated with a calibration curve spiked at 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100 µg L−1 in the pooled sample of brain (final extract). In addition, the same calibration curve (0.1, 0.5, 1, 10, 50, 100 µg L−1) was prepared in solvent (water/methanol, 1:1, v/v) to evaluate matrix effect.•Matrix effect (ME%).
